shortDescription: Office visit, established patient (minimal)
plainEnglishDescription: The simplest type of office visit for a patient who has seen this doctor before. Typically involves very brief check-ins that may not even require a physician, such as a nurse measuring blood pressure or giving a simple injection.
insuranceNotes: Lowest-level office visit code. Usually covered with minimal copay.

shortDescription: Office visit, established patient (brief)
plainEnglishDescription: A brief office visit for a patient who has seen this doctor before. This is a straightforward visit, typically 10-19 minutes, for simple health issues that don't require extensive evaluation.
insuranceNotes: Lower copay than 99213. Appropriate for simple, quick visits.

shortDescription: Office visit, established patient
plainEnglishDescription: A standard office visit for a patient who has seen this doctor before. The visit typically takes 15-29 minutes and involves checking on an existing health issue, discussing symptoms, and possibly adjusting treatment. This is the most commonly billed office visit code.
insuranceNotes: Most insurance plans cover this as a standard office visit with your regular copay.
misuseWarning: This code is sometimes 'upcoded' to 99214, which costs more. If your visit was brief and straightforward, you may be able to dispute an upgrade.

shortDescription: Office visit, established patient (extended)
plainEnglishDescription: An extended office visit for an established patient. This is used when the doctor spends more time (30-39 minutes) due to a more complex health issue that requires detailed evaluation and decision-making.
insuranceNotes: Higher copay than 99213. Verify the complexity of your visit justified this code.

shortDescription: Office visit, established patient (comprehensive)
plainEnglishDescription: The most extensive office visit for an established patient. Used for highly complex medical situations requiring 40-54 minutes of physician time. Involves thorough examination, complex decision-making, and often multiple conditions being addressed.
insuranceNotes: Highest-level established patient visit. Should only be used for genuinely complex cases.
misuseWarning: Review your visit - this high-level code should reflect significant time and complexity.

shortDescription: Office visit, new patient
plainEnglishDescription: A standard office visit for someone seeing this doctor for the first time. Takes 30-44 minutes and includes taking your medical history, examining you, and discussing initial treatment options.
commonUses: First visit with a new doctor
insuranceNotes: New patient visits cost more than established patient visits. This is normal.

shortDescription: CT scan, head/brain, without contrast
plainEnglishDescription: A computed tomography (CT) scan of your head and brain without using contrast dye. This creates detailed cross-sectional images to check for injuries, bleeding, tumors, or other abnormalities in the brain.
insuranceNotes: May require prior authorization. Emergency room scans typically covered at emergency rates.

shortDescription: CT scan, head/brain, with contrast
plainEnglishDescription: A CT scan of your head and brain using contrast dye injected into your bloodstream. The dye helps highlight blood vessels and certain abnormalities that might not be visible on a regular CT scan.
insuranceNotes: Includes cost of contrast material. May require prior authorization.

shortDescription: Chest X-ray, 2 views
plainEnglishDescription: A standard chest X-ray with two views (typically front and side). Used to examine your lungs, heart, and chest area for conditions like pneumonia, heart problems, or injuries.
insuranceNotes: Usually covered as a basic diagnostic test. Often lower cost at outpatient facilities.

shortDescription: X-ray, ankle, complete
plainEnglishDescription: A complete X-ray examination of the ankle, including multiple views (typically 3 images). Used to check for fractures, dislocations, arthritis, or other bone and joint problems.
insuranceNotes: Usually covered as a diagnostic test. May have lower cost at outpatient imaging centers vs. hospital.

shortDescription: X-ray, foot, complete
plainEnglishDescription: A complete X-ray of the foot with multiple views (typically 3 images). Used to check for fractures, bone spurs, arthritis, or other problems in the foot bones.
insuranceNotes: Usually covered with standard imaging copay.

shortDescription: Electrocardiogram (ECG/EKG), complete
plainEnglishDescription: A complete electrocardiogram that records the electrical activity of your heart. This includes placing sensors on your chest, recording the heart rhythm, and having a doctor interpret the results.
insuranceNotes: Usually covered with minimal copay as a diagnostic test.

shortDescription: ECG tracing only
plainEnglishDescription: Just the technical component of an EKG - the actual recording of your heart's electrical activity. Does not include the doctor's interpretation, which is billed separately.
insuranceNotes: Often paired with 93010 for interpretation. Together they equal 93000.
misuseWarning: Should not be billed with 93000. If you see both, question the bill.

shortDescription: Rapid COVID-19 test
plainEnglishDescription: A rapid diagnostic test for detecting SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) virus. Results are typically available within 15-30 minutes using a nasal swab sample.
insuranceNotes: Many insurers cover COVID testing at no cost. Check your plan's current policy.

shortDescription: COVID-19 PCR test
plainEnglishDescription: A molecular (PCR) test for COVID-19 that detects the virus's genetic material. More accurate than rapid tests but takes longer to get results (usually 1-3 days).
insuranceNotes: May be covered at no cost depending on your insurance and current policies.

shortDescription: Comprehensive metabolic panel
plainEnglishDescription: A blood test that measures 14 different substances in your blood, including glucose, calcium, electrolytes, and kidney/liver function markers. Provides a broad picture of your body's chemical balance and metabolism.
insuranceNotes: Usually covered as preventive care or diagnostic. May be bundled with other labs.

shortDescription: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential
plainEnglishDescription: A common blood test that counts your red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Also shows the different types of white blood cells. Helps detect infections, anemia, and many other conditions.
insuranceNotes: One of the most common lab tests. Usually covered with minimal or no copay.

shortDescription: Blood draw (venipuncture)
plainEnglishDescription: The procedure of drawing blood from a vein, typically from your arm, using a needle. This is the collection process only - the actual tests on the blood are billed separately.
insuranceNotes: Small fee added to lab work. Should only appear once per blood draw session.
misuseWarning: You should only see this once per visit, not for each test performed on the blood.

shortDescription: Acute upper respiratory infection
plainEnglishDescription: A diagnosis code for common upper respiratory infections like the common cold. This indicates an infection affecting your nose, sinuses, throat, or upper airways that came on suddenly.
insuranceNotes: This is a diagnosis code, not a procedure. It appears on bills to explain why you received treatment.

shortDescription: Low back pain
plainEnglishDescription: A diagnosis code for pain in the lower back region. This is one of the most common diagnosis codes used for back pain complaints without a specific identified cause.
insuranceNotes: Diagnosis code only. Treatments will be billed separately with procedure codes.

shortDescription: Type 2 diabetes without complications
plainEnglishDescription: A diagnosis code for Type 2 diabetes mellitus without any complications documented. This is the basic diagnosis code for adult-onset diabetes that is being managed without current complications.
insuranceNotes: Chronic condition diagnosis. Many diabetes supplies and monitoring may be covered.

shortDescription: Essential hypertension (high blood pressure)
plainEnglishDescription: A diagnosis code for primary high blood pressure without a specific identifiable cause. This is the most common form of hypertension and one of the most frequently used diagnosis codes.
insuranceNotes: Chronic condition. Blood pressure medications and monitoring usually covered.

shortDescription: Blood glucose test strips (50)
plainEnglishDescription: A box of 50 blood glucose test strips used with a glucose meter to monitor blood sugar levels at home. Essential supply for people managing diabetes.
insuranceNotes: Usually covered for diabetics. Check if your meter brand requires specific strips.

shortDescription: CPAP machine
plainEnglishDescription: A continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) device used to treat sleep apnea. The machine delivers steady air pressure through a mask to keep airways open during sleep.
insuranceNotes: Often rented before purchase. Requires sleep study diagnosis. May need prior authorization.

shortDescription: Immunization administration (first vaccine)
plainEnglishDescription: The fee for administering the first vaccine injection during a visit. This covers the nurse's time and supplies for giving you the shot - the vaccine itself is billed separately.
insuranceNotes: Many preventive vaccines are covered at 100%. Administration fee may still apply.

shortDescription: Flu vaccine, quadrivalent
plainEnglishDescription: The flu vaccine itself (not the administration). Quadrivalent means it protects against four strains of influenza. This is the actual vaccine product cost.
insuranceNotes: Preventive flu vaccines are typically covered at 100% under ACA plans.

shortDescription: Office visit, new patient (brief)
plainEnglishDescription: A brief office visit for a new patient, typically 10 minutes. Basic evaluation for straightforward problems.
insuranceNotes: Entry-level new patient visit.

shortDescription: Office visit, new patient (straightforward)
plainEnglishDescription: A straightforward office visit for a new patient requiring straightforward medical decision making.
insuranceNotes: Standard new patient visit.

shortDescription: Office visit, new patient (moderate complexity)
plainEnglishDescription: A comprehensive new patient visit requiring moderate medical decision making, typically 45-59 minutes.
insuranceNotes: Higher-level new patient visit for complex cases.

shortDescription: Office visit, new patient (high complexity)
plainEnglishDescription: The most comprehensive new patient visit requiring high complexity medical decision making, 60-74 minutes.
insuranceNotes: Highest-level new patient visit.

shortDescription: Emergency department visit (minor)
plainEnglishDescription: Emergency department visit for a self-limited or minor problem.
insuranceNotes: Lowest-level ER visit.

shortDescription: Emergency department visit (low severity)
plainEnglishDescription: Emergency department visit for a problem of low to moderate severity.

shortDescription: Emergency department visit (moderate severity)
plainEnglishDescription: Emergency department visit for a problem of moderate severity.

shortDescription: Emergency department visit (high severity)
plainEnglishDescription: Emergency department visit for a problem of high severity requiring urgent evaluation.

shortDescription: Emergency department visit (highest severity)
plainEnglishDescription: Emergency department visit for a problem requiring immediate significant intervention or posing an immediate threat to life.

shortDescription: CT scan, chest, without contrast
plainEnglishDescription: Computed tomography (CT) scan of the chest without contrast dye. Provides detailed images of lungs and chest structures.

shortDescription: CT scan, abdomen and pelvis, without contrast
plainEnglishDescription: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis without contrast material. Evaluates abdominal organs, kidneys, and pelvic structures.

shortDescription: CT scan, abdomen and pelvis, with contrast
plainEnglishDescription: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast dye injection. Better visualization of blood vessels and organs.

shortDescription: MRI, brain, with and without contrast
plainEnglishDescription: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain with and without contrast material. Detailed brain imaging without radiation.

shortDescription: MRI, lumbar spine, without contrast
plainEnglishDescription: MRI of the lower back (lumbar spine) without contrast. Evaluates disc problems, nerve compression, and spinal conditions.

shortDescription: MRI, knee, without contrast
plainEnglishDescription: MRI of the knee joint without contrast. Evaluates meniscus, ligaments, cartilage, and joint structures.

shortDescription: Lipid panel
plainEnglishDescription: Blood test measuring cholesterol levels including total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides.

shortDescription: TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone)
plainEnglishDescription: Blood test to check thyroid function by measuring TSH levels.

shortDescription: Hemoglobin A1c
plainEnglishDescription: Blood test measuring average blood sugar over 2-3 months. Key test for diabetes management.

shortDescription: Total knee replacement
plainEnglishDescription: Surgical procedure to replace the knee joint with an artificial joint (prosthesis).

shortDescription: Total hip replacement
plainEnglishDescription: Surgical procedure to replace the hip joint with an artificial joint.

shortDescription: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy
plainEnglishDescription: Minimally invasive surgical removal of the gallbladder using small incisions and a camera.

shortDescription: Laparoscopic appendectomy
plainEnglishDescription: Minimally invasive surgical removal of the appendix.

shortDescription: Echocardiogram, complete
plainEnglishDescription: Ultrasound examination of the heart including Doppler flow studies. Shows heart structure and function.

shortDescription: Cardiac catheterization, coronary angiography
plainEnglishDescription: Procedure inserting a catheter into heart arteries to visualize blockages using contrast dye.

shortDescription: Panniculitis, unspecified
plainEnglishDescription: Inflammation of the fatty tissue under the skin.

shortDescription: Pneumonia, unspecified organism
plainEnglishDescription: Diagnosis code for lung infection (pneumonia) when the specific cause is not identified.

shortDescription: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
plainEnglishDescription: Diagnosis code for urinary tract infection (UTI).

shortDescription: GERD with esophagitis
plainEnglishDescription: Gastroesophageal reflux disease with inflammation of the esophagus.

plainEnglishDescription: Diagnosis code for depression - single episode.

plainEnglishDescription: Diagnosis code for chronic anxiety that is not tied to a specific cause.
